metrics_guide.title: DORA’s software delivery performance metrics
metrics_guide.model: Five metrics in two factors: throughput and instability (replaces the earlier 'four keys').

metrics.name: Change lead time
metrics.definition_paraphrase: Elapsed time for a change to travel from being committed to version control to running in production.

metrics.name: Deployment frequency
metrics.definition_paraphrase: Count of deployments within a period, or alternatively the interval between deployments.

metrics.name: Failed deployment recovery time
metrics.definition_paraphrase: How long it takes to recover after a deployment fails and needs immediate intervention. Replaced MTTR / time to restore service in 2023 so that only change-induced failures count. Note: the current guide lists it under throughput; the history page also groups it with throughput.

metrics.name: Change fail rate
metrics.definition_paraphrase: Proportion of deployments that need immediate intervention afterwards, typically a rollback or hotfix.

metrics.name: Deployment rework rate
metrics.definition_paraphrase: Proportion of deployments that are unplanned and occur because of a production incident. Introduced as the fifth metric in 2024.

historical_names.paraphrase: 2014 used deployment frequency, lead time for changes, MTTR and change fail rate (CFR excluded from the 2014 construct statistically); 2015 grouped throughput vs stability; 2018 added availability (SDO performance); 2021 availability broadened to reliability (described as operational, not delivery, performance); 2023 MTTR renamed/redefined as failed deployment recovery time; 2024 added deployment rework rate, giving five metrics in throughput and instability factors.

usage_cautions: Do not turn metrics into targets (Goodhart's law); mandates like 'everyone deploys daily' invite gaming. [Common pitfalls: Setting metrics as a goal]
Do not rely on a single metric; use several, some deliberately in tension. [Having one metric to rule them all]
Do not use industry or regulation as an excuse not to improve. [Using industry as a shield against improving]
Apply at the application/service level; comparing very different applications (e.g. mobile app vs mainframe) misleads. [Making disparate comparisons]
Share all five metrics across dev, ops and release rather than assigning metrics to silos. [Having siloed ownership]
Aim to improve your own team over time, not to compete with other teams or organisations. [Competing]
Do not over-invest in precise measurement plumbing at the expense of improvement; conversations or the Quick Check may suffice to start. [Focusing on measurement at the expense of improvement]
Context matters: blending metrics across teams or a whole organisation can be problematic because contexts differ. [Key insights]
Metrics are best suited to one application or service at a time. [Key insights]
